relations.statement: Every inhabitant of the sealed isomorphism preserves the numbers of data and forms, with no hypothesis.
From a clean base no class that has been left is reached again.
From a clean base, a revisited class is the very regime reached by unchanging events, so recurrence is only a stutter.

lemmas.statement: Two clean regimes (well-formed, no list holding an entry twice) related by the isomorphism have all five component counts equal.
From a clean base, the counts of a history are functions of the class it reaches.

near_misses.claim: Dropping either the well-formed or the clean hypothesis still gives equal counts for instances, rules or requirements.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Six exhibited pairs show neither hypothesis can be dropped.

near_misses.claim: Across two bases, the class determines the count.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The class does not carry the count across two bases.
